blocks.text: The siege narrative sharpens here when Abdali refuses to ignore the taunts coming from the Jat stronghold at Koel and insists that he will not proceed farther until the fort is mastered. To him the drumming and bravado from inside are proof that the Jats were poking fun at him, so the campaign becomes a test of prestige as much as a military necessity.

As his officers review the problem, the fort stocked with plenty of provisions is described as difficult to reduce by ordinary means. Its defenders are well supplied, the position is strong, and the discussion makes clear that a prolonged effort may be required before the road to Agra can be secured.

Abdali therefore turns to studied siegecraft rather than impulse, consulting a book that dealt with the art of breaking forts and asking for the stronghold to be mapped precisely. He got a complete sketch design of the targeted fort traced so that the next move would be systematic and overwhelming.
